prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: offshore wind farm operation/maintenance for reliable generation, personnel safety, asset integrity; lifecycle spans commissioning/acceptance, routine operation, refurbishment, decommissioning. Boundary includes turbine structures/array, Offshore Substation, export connection through Grid Interface Relay (external-grid interface), marine/shore facilities, personnel, maintenance, and participating external organizations. Excludes public-grid assets beyond agreed connection and unrelated port operations.

Canonical names identify parts, actors, states, controlled items. Aliases: Glassfin = Turbine Controller; Morrowick = Offshore Substation; Pale Lantern = Weather Service.

Elements: Turbine Controller controls an individual turbine; Pitch System and Rotor Brake Unit are turbine subsystems; Converter Cabinet and Nacelle Condition Monitor are distinct turbine equipment for maintenance/condition review; Turbine Sensor Bus is included. Blade Inspection Drone assesses turbine blades. Offshore Substation provides offshore electrical collection/switching; Main Transformer is a substation asset; Export Cable Monitor is an export-system asset. SCADA Gateway provides supervisory monitoring/control interface. Shore Control Room houses authorized personnel, continuously monitors, and coordinates dispatch. Fleet Dispatch Console coordinates resources; Maintenance Planning Engine prepares/sequences maintenance.

Marine coordination: Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, Helideck, applicable vessel procedures. Access/workforce interfaces: North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner, Personnel Tracking Console. Inventory/replenishment: Warehouse System, Spares Hub. External interfaces: Weather Service, Metocean Buoy (offshore environmental-observation source), grid dispatch, port support, emergency response organizations. Enabling functions: cybersecurity, communications, fire protection, backup power. No specific item flows or modes stated.

Requirements: authorize work, control hazards, account for personnel/vessels; prevent pollution, minimize marine disturbance, promptly respond to environmental incidents. Availability relies on monitoring, timely fault response, planned maintenance, coordinated access. Commissioning requires documented handover/verification to operations. Decisions use validated status, approved procedures, current forecasts, grid instructions. Maintenance considers condition, resources, access, production; unplanned work requires prioritized assessment/controlled mobilization proportional to severity. Decommissioning supports safe isolation, removal planning, residual-record transfer to responsible organization.

New part:
S045: Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, and Service Operations Vessel represent marine resources that may support offshore work.
S046: Helideck is included as an access facility for activities supported by helicopter operations.
S047: Personnel Tracking Console represents the personnel location and accountability function.
S048: Warehouse System and Spares Hub represent the inventory and logistics context for maintenance materials.
S049: Work Permit Portal and Cybersecurity Gateway represent enabling functions that support controlled and secure operations.
S050: The operating concept also recognizes grid, emergency response, communications, and port support as external or enabling capabilities.
S051: The system architecture separates offshore equipment, operational services, and shore-based decision functions while preserving defined interfaces between them.
S052: The SCADA Gateway provides a controlled boundary for supervisory data exchange between offshore assets and shore-based operations.
S053: For this concept, SCADA Gateway is designated Juniper Vale as its operational alias.
S054: The Maintenance Planning Engine supports work preparation by organizing maintenance needs, resource considerations, and planning constraints.
S055: For this concept, Maintenance Planning Engine is designated Thistle Crown as its operational alias.
S056: The Shore Control Room is the principal shore-based setting for monitoring and coordinating wind farm operations.
S057: For this concept, Shore Control Room is designated Amber Quay as its operational alias.
S058: These three components have distinct responsibilities and are treated as cooperating parts of one operational system.
S059: The SCADA Gateway mediates supervisory exchanges and supports consistent access to operational information.
S060: The Turbine Controller performs local turbine control functions within the offshore equipment environment.
S061: The Turbine Controller produces the Pitch Deviation Notice for operational handling.
S062: The SCADA Engineer maintains the configuration and technical integrity of supervisory interfaces.
S063: The Control Engineer uses the shore-based operational picture to assess equipment status and coordinate response.
S064: The Shore Control Room provides a shared operational context for personnel responsible for offshore assets.
S065: The Duty Planner uses the Maintenance Planning Engine to prepare and review maintenance activities.
S066: The Maintenance Planning Engine supports planning decisions without replacing the judgment of the Duty Planner.
S067: The Weather Service contributes environmental information to operational planning and coordination.
S068: The Marine Coordinator considers offshore conditions and vessel availability when coordinating access to work sites.
S069: The Fleet Dispatch Console provides a fleet-level view of dispatch activity for operational coordination.
S070: The Work Permit Portal supports authorization processes that govern work under controlled conditions.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
